names.name: Dhul-Qarnayn
names.morph: Construct phrase: ذو (possessor of) + القرنين (the two horns); used in the Qur'an as a title.
names.short: Qur'anic title meaning “the possessor of the two horns”
names.primary: Dhul-Qarnayn (ذو القرنين, “the possessor of the two horns”) is the title by which the Qur'an refers to a righteous monarch whose story is told in Surah al-Kahf (18:83–98). The Qur'an gives a title rather than a personal name, and the historical identification of the figure is disputed among exegetes and historians. As a given name it is rare and usually commemorative.
names.explain: The expression is a construct (iḍāfa) of ذو “possessor of” and القرنين “the two horns”. The Qur'an uses it as a title, not as a personal name, and does not explain the epithet. Classical explanations include two locks of hair, two horns, two eras, or rule over east and west; this record reports the disagreement without adopting a speculative identification.
names.qnote: The title appears in Qur'an 18:83–98, where the narrative of Dhul-Qarnayn is related; the Qur'an does not give a personal name or a definitive historical identification.
names.rel_status: A Qur'anic title, not a divine name or a prophetic name established by the Qur'an.
names.rel_explain: The Qur'an presents Dhul-Qarnayn as a righteous ruler in the al-Kahf narrative. Classical scholars debated his identity and whether he was a prophet; this record asserts neither.

names.hist_note: Ibn Hisham's Sirah and Ibn Sa'd's Tabaqat record Shayba ibn Hashim's life and the origin of the name Abd al-Muttalib.
